instruction:
Morph Target Three-State Export

look at scene.obj. It contains a ZBrush Tool whose first (and only) SubTool, named Head, is a smooth head-shaped ellipsoid polymesh at approximately 2000 quads (32 lat x 64 lon with triangle caps; Y stretched by 1.3). It has a single default polygroup, no UVs, and no polypaint.

Load this OBJ into ZBrush, use the Morph Target feature to capture three discrete states of a cheek-dent sculpt, and export them to `baseline.obj`, `edited.obj`, and `partial.obj`. All three must share identical vertex and face counts.

The three exported OBJs must satisfy:

- Each contains exactly one SubTool named Head, and all three share identical vertex and face counts.
- baseline.obj matches the input scene.obj vertex-for-vertex within 1e-5 BU.
- edited.obj differs from baseline.obj by at least 0.04 BU at the maximum displacement vertex.
- partial.obj equals edited.obj within 0.01 BU for every vertex with y > 0.2, and equals baseline.obj within 0.01 BU for every vertex with y <= 0.2.
- All three meshes are manifold.
